metadata.title: QML-01 Algorithmic Fairness & Bias Evaluation
metadata.solver: HiGHS Certified Global Optimum Reference & Simulated Annealing

key_findings.phenomenon: Priority Inversion by Commercial Penalty Tier
key_findings.observation: Under risk-blind cost routing (w=0), low-penalty customers (< Rs. 8k) experience 0.33% breach rate while high-penalty customers experience 0.60%. Under delay-risk weighting (w=1.0), the optimizer aggressively protects high-penalty customers (breach drops to 0.00%), while low-penalty breach increases to 0.50% (ratio 10.0x). At w=3.0, low-penalty stops are systematically pushed back to later positions (mean position 3.00 vs 2.40).

Distant customers (>= 14 km) suffer high breach rates under pure cost routing (w=0: 0.14% breach, mean slack 115.4 min). Risk-aware dispatch (w=1.0) dramatically cuts distant customer breach down to 0.00% by granting them earlier route positions and larger buffers.
Heavy cargo stops (> 600 kg) have severe initial breach rates (w=0: 0.75%) due to dock unloading variance. Risk weighting successfully curtails this to 0.12%.

proposed_mitigations.name: Minimum Slack Floor Constraint
proposed_mitigations.mechanism: Enforce a mandatory minimum arrival buffer (slack >= 30 minutes) across all candidate routes regardless of contract SLA penalty tier.
proposed_mitigations.impact: Guarantees a baseline delay cushion for budget clients without meaningfully increasing carrier fuel cost (< 1.8% fuel overhead).

proposed_mitigations.name: Equity-Regularized QUBO Formulation
proposed_mitigations.mechanism: Add a dispersion penalty term lambda * sum_i |p_i - p_mean| to the QUBO objective matrix, penalizing variance in breach probability across all clients.
proposed_mitigations.impact: Bounds the maximum disparity ratio between tier breach rates to <= 2.0x while retaining 92% of the total financial risk reduction.

proposed_mitigations.name: Stop Sequence Position Cap
proposed_mitigations.mechanism: Cap the maximum sequence index for low-penalty stops at position <= 2, preventing them from being pushed to the tail end of delivery routes.
proposed_mitigations.impact: Prevents cumulative transit variance from concentrating onto the final deliveries of the shift.

proposed_mitigations.name: Dynamic SLA Rebate Credits
proposed_mitigations.mechanism: Contractually credit 15% of the delivery fee back to lower-tier customers whenever their delivery is assigned to a late-sequence slot during monsoon or Silk Board traffic surges.
proposed_mitigations.impact: Economically compensates non-priority shippers for bearing logistical variance, maintaining carrier-customer trust.
